title: Did I Choose the Wrong Move?
captions: My ex just texted: ‘If you don’t answer in 5 minutes, I’ll kill the kid.’ #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #thriller #ex
I hear a knock, the clock ticks, and the police are still miles away. #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #tension #call
The truth is darker than I imagined. Who’s really in danger? #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #twist #verdict
parts: [[5 MIN LEFT]] My ex just texted: ‘If you don’t answer in five minutes, I’ll kill the kid.’ My heart slams. I stare at the phone, the screen glowing like a warning light. [[9:47 PM · LIVING ROOM]] I hear the baby monitor crackle, a faint giggle that could be my niece or a recorded loop. I glance at the hallway, the floorboards creak under my weight. [[RULE 1 · CALL POLICE]] My fingers tremble, dialing 9‑1‑1. The operator’s voice is calm, but the timer in my head is louder. I whisper, “It’s my ex. She’s threatening my child.” The line clicks, “Stay on the line.” [[3 MINUTES LEFT]] A car alarm blares outside, distant sirens wail. My phone buzzes again—another message: “Don’t waste time.” I grip the edge of the couch, feeling the cheap plastic bite my palm. The baby monitor suddenly goes silent, replaced by static. My mind races. If I stay, she might act. If I run, I might lose the kid. [[RULE 2 · NOTIFY FRIENDS]] I shout into the empty house, “Help! Someone’s in the house!” My voice echoes, bouncing off the walls, while the clock ticks down. Then, a soft click— the front door unlocks. I hold my breath, waiting for the next move.

[[10 MIN LATER]] The police are still on their way, but the minutes feel like hours. I stay crouched behind the couch, eyes glued to the door. My ex’s voice crackles through the monitor, “You always think you’re smarter.” I swallow hard, trying not to gasp. [[9:55 PM · KITCHEN]] I hear footsteps on the tile, slow, deliberate. A shadow slips under the door crack, then stops. My pulse hammers. I clutch the phone, thumb hovering over the emergency button. The baby monitor flickers, a grainy image of a small hand reaching for a toy appears. I gasp. [[RULE 3 · NO NEGOTIATION]] I whisper, “What do you want?” The voice replies, “Just watch.” The door handle turns, metal grinding. I brace for a burst of violence, but the door opens to empty hallway. No one is there. My breath comes in short bursts. I glance at the monitor—now it shows a dark room, a single red light blinking. My mind spins. Did she set a trap? [[5 MIN LEFT]] I hear a faint beep from my phone, a live‑location ping. I glance, my location flashing on a map. Something is moving toward me. I stare at the monitor, the red light pulsing like a heart. The sound of a camera click echoes, louder than my own thoughts. I realize the kid might not be a child at all.

[[FINAL MINUTES]] The police finally burst through the front door, guns drawn, shouting commands. I stand, hands raised, the baby monitor clutched like a lifeline. The officer’s flashlight lands on the monitor, revealing a tiny, hidden camera peeking from behind a fake plant. My ex’s voice crackles one last time, “You should have answered, but now everyone will see.” The realization hits like a punch: the ‘kid’ was never a child, it was a recording device she planted to frame me for a murder she just committed. I glance at the screen—there, in grainy black‑and‑white, a shadowy figure lunges at a man in a hallway, a knife glinting. My ex’s silhouette appears behind the camera, smirking. The officer turns to me, “We’ve got you on video, ma’am.” I feel the weight of the decision I made, calling the police instead of negotiating. Did I save a life or condemn an innocent? The camera’s red light blinks one final time. I stare at the screen, heart pounding, and ask you: Was I right to call the police and risk the child’s life, or should I have tried to bargain with a manipulative ex? #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #twist #verdict
